correctness.rationale: The S6 action is transitive on unordered disjoint pairs, so deletion of the edge 12–34 suffices. I rebuilt both open-neighborhood complexes by testing all nonempty subsets of the fifteen vertices for a common neighbor and independently replayed CERTIFICATE.json, rather than executing the supplied verifier. The face counts are 710 and 660 with the claimed f-vectors. I checked the 268 absolute collapses, the 53 incident disjoint pairs on the residual 124 faces, and topologically sorted the full reversed Hasse graph. The unmatched cells are exactly one vertex and 17 triangles; Forman's CW model therefore has 17 two-cells attached to the point. I also replayed the 22 relative cancellations and obtained the signed boundary with rows (-1,-1,0,0) and (0,0,-1,-1). Independently, writing X=N(K) and Y=N(K-e), the relative chains split into the parts lost from each of the two endpoint-neighborhood simplices (these simplices intersect in the vertex 56, retained in Y). For the first simplex on the pairs from {3,4,5,6}, a face is lost exactly if it contains 34 and its union uses all four labels: otherwise a second common neighbor can be chosen using a missing label and 1, or 12 itself is still a neighbor. Its intersection with Y is the simplex omitting 34 plus the cones from 34 on the two disjoint edges {35,45} and {36,46}; collapsing one side of each triangle gives a contractible base with a single loop attached via the cone vertex, hence homotopy type S^1. The other simplex is symmetric. Thus H3(X,Y)=0 and H2(X,Y)=Z^2 over the integers, in agreement with the cancellation check. The pair sequence and H1(Y)=0 give the claimed injection and free cokernel. No general Kneser edge-deletion claim is inferred.

value.rationale: A one-edge fault in the first triangle-bearing two-subset Kneser graph is a natural minimal graph perturbation. A complete integral homotopy computation and a primitive inclusion distinguish the effect of that fault from mere loss of Euler characteristic or Betti rank. The precise retained subgroup property is useful in comparing graph-fault stages, without claiming a general stability theorem.
